reasoning_traces.think:
The capitalization rate (r_c) represents the technical ratio of converting present goods into future income, forming a core operational definition in the theory of investment. This ratio is fundamentally tied to productivity, linking the value of capital goods produced to the value of present goods consumed. Inflationary processes, however, do not create new purchasing power but instead redistribute existing purchasing power among agents. The mechanism operates through the issuance of new currency via bank loans, which increases the nominal supply of capital and lowers interest rates. These primitives form a dual structure: one describing static capital formation and another describing dynamic monetary redistribution. The failure mode arises when these two systems are misaligned—when loan creation outpaces productive capacity, leading to speculative bubbles or deflationary spirals. The psychological component introduces non-linear feedback loops, where expectations of future returns can amplify or dampen current capital flows, complicating deterministic modeling.
